summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and J-tube dependence was admitted due to a clogged feeding tube, fever, hypotension, and tachycardia. He was found to have sepsis likely from acute tracheitis, with sputum cultures showing sparse growth of multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii complex, sensitive to gentamicin. He also had acute kidney injury and hypernatremia, which resolved with IV fluids. Liver transaminases were elevated, but ultrasound showed only cholelithiasis without acute cholecystitis. He was treated with IV piperacillin-tazobactam and gentamicin. A PICC line was placed on hospital day 4 for outpatient antibiotic completion. His respiratory status improved, and he was weaned from supplemental oxygen. Urinary retention was managed with a short-term catheter. He stabilized and was discharged back to the nursing home with a 6-day course of IV antibiotics, detailed care instructions, and follow-up plans.
problems: Acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase and lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
